Grangeclare West and Dancing City are others for the shortlist.

selections.comment: FRANCISCO is interesting. He was slowly away upped to 7f last time at Chelmsford and never got near the action before coasting home. Prior to that he was placed over 6f here and looked as if the extra furlong here should suit (his first two career runs came over 7f and are just about his best pieces of form). With scope for a little improvement he's worth chancing in a trappy but weak affair. Yeoman should offer tough opposition. He's been in decent form this year and is switched back to the AW after a solid 4th of 21 at Doncaster on turf a few weeks ago. All three career wins have come here and although they were over 1m the drop back to 7f is worth a try as he's tackled the trip just twice before, on career debut on heavy ground and at Southwell last September where he was placed staying on late. Jermey Fanshawe's gelding is not immune from a tardy start but if he can break on terms he'd have every chance. Autumn Festival is feared off a lowly mark of 55 here compared to 72 which he ran off two runs back on turf. He wasn't beaten far when placed last time at Kempton showing a bit more than of late and can get involved again. Sybil Charm has solid credentials and is another to consider but has looked better over 6f of late

It's wortyh another try as he's shaped as if a mile should suit, and given a more positive ride can serve it up to the selection

selections.comment: Fine Print sets the bar and arrives in top order having landed a class 6 handicap here over 1m6f to open his account. The step up to 2m could bring out a little improvement but he's likely to be a bit skinny in the market given his maiden victory took 19 attempts. He's taken on by SOPHAR SOGOOD who went much better on his third run this year getting close to peak levels. He's now back at his last winning trip and can continue the progress to land a 7th career victory. Scylla has been in decent form for much of this year and can fill the frame

selections.comment: RIYADH GEM looks best placed to land the spoils. Archie Watson's colt opened his account on nursery debut when last seen in November. He stayed on powerfully that day over 1m and this extra couple of furlongs looks well within his compass. Most of the field hold a fitness edge but if ready to go off the 156 day layoff he can keep the ball rolling and double-up. Must Believe has the form to go close and is feared most but he has to bounce back from a poor effort last time. There are excuses for that below par effort given he was unable to get involved from a wide draw and if showing his sole effort on Tapeta to be an anomaly he should ber bang there at the business end. Zizi could offer a bit of each way value. Her return to action earlier this month was abysmal but it came over in adequate 7f and she never figured. She had prevoiusly opened her account in a maiden event here over 1m and the step up in trip looks right up her street. A much imoproved effort is on the cards
